transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15 16:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (VP Eng - Celestia), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Infra)

Summary: quick integration discovery focused on how Celestia would integrate Redwood's Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options into their LangChain / LlamaIndex pipelines; discuss SDKs, gateway/proxy approach, rate limits, and observability hooks. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off. I'm Sofia, I'm the AE here at Redwood, joining with Marcus our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Alex: Good, thanks Sofia. Excited to dig in, we just want to make sure integration overheads aren't going to be a huge lift.
[00:18] Sofia: Totally, that's the focus today. We'll run through SDKs, LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns, and then get into network/gateway options and observability. Marcus, do you want to start with the SDK story?
[00:27] Marcus: Sure, quick overview — Redwood has first-class REST + official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. The Python SDK meshes directly with langchain via the LLM wrapper we publish, and we have example notebooks and a LlamaIndex connector (sometimes docs say 'LamaIndex' in older samples, apologies). Link I just posted in chat: https://redwood.internal/docs/sdk-langchain (note: shared deck will be in email).
[00:48] Priya: Cool, do you maintain the LangChain wrapper upstream or is it a community piece? We use an older LangChain version, currently pinned to 0.0.240.
[00:58] Marcus: We maintain an official wrapper and try to keep compatibility across LangChain minor versions; for pinned versions we provide sample glue code. For LlamaIndex we have a connector that supports vector store callbacks and streaming chunks into an embedding pipeline. There are occasional naming mismatches in older guides — you'll see LlamaIndex spelled differently in a couple examples.
[01:20] Tom: From infra side our main questions are around the gateway/proxy approach. We already have an internal gateway that mTLSs outbound traffic; can Redwood sit behind that or do we need a separate proxy?
[01:30] Marcus: Two common patterns: 1) call Redwood's hosted API through your gateway/proxy with standard TLS/mTLS — works fine and won't require egress whitelisting more than our API endpoints; 2) for more control you can run Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with a customer-dedicated endpoint and optionally an internal sidecar proxy. The VPC option supports VPC peering and private link styles.
[01:55] Alex: And latency difference between hosted and dedicated? We're latency-sensitive for one feature — real-time chat with ~150ms token latency target.
[02:05] Marcus: Typical hosted P95 can be ~200-350ms for open models depending on model size and seq length; Dedicated on colocated HW and pinned models can often meet your 120-150ms target, assuming you provision the right pool (we recommend benchmark runs). We'll share benchmarks; note caching (prefix/KV cache) and batching behavior also impacts per-token time.
[02:35] Priya: When you say KV cache, do you mean the attention KV cache or a prefix cache? We have concerns about context reuse between requests.
[02:44] Marcus: Good callout — Redwood supports both. Prefix caching stores common prompts and reduces compute; KV cache is the transformer KV cache used during generation. We expose hooks to control cache TTLs and invalidation; for strict privacy you'd turn off shared prefix caching on Dedicated/Private.
[03:04] Alex: Security questions — we need SOC2, SSO, SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. How mature are those for hosted vs private?
[03:13] Sofia: Hosted is SOC2-compliant and supports SSO/SAML and customer-managed KMS for secrets (via integration). We also provide audit logs and token-level tracing in Console. For the Private option you run a customer-controlled control plane with HSM/KMS integration as part of the deployment; we'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 report after the call.
[03:36] Tom: For Private, do we need to open ports or can we peer? Our security team prefers peering rather than open egress.
[03:43] Marcus: We support VPC peering and private connectivity; no open internet required for Dedicated/Private. We'll include network diagrams in the follow-up.
[03:56] Alex: Great. On quotas and rate limits — we have burst-y workloads at month end, plus steady traffic. Can you do per-route quotas and token budget controls?
[04:07] Marcus: Yes, rate limits can be applied at API key, route, and model level. For Dedicated we can implement per-tenant shaping with burst buckets. For Hosted you can request quota increases or purchase reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
[04:24] Priya: Do you expose rate-limit headers we can programmatically react to? We need to implement client-side backoff in langchain wrappers.
[04:31] Marcus: Absolutely, we expose standard X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After headers and a JSON error body with suggested backoff. The SDKs surface those as exceptions.
[04:40] Alex: Observability — we need tracing into our existing Jaeger/Splunk stack. Any integrations?
[04:47] Marcus: Redwood Console emits structured logs and supports trace export via OpenTelemetry. You can ingest traces into Jaeger/Datadog; we also provide route-level token costing and per-request metadata via headers for observability hooks.
[05:04] Tom: How do you tag calls for billing versus tracing? We want to separate production vs dev usage in our cost dashboards.
[05:11] Marcus: API keys map to billing project IDs and you can set metadata headers (x-redwood-project, x-redwood-environment) — Console and the billing export include that.
[05:22] Priya: On the client integration side, we use LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). How seamless is streaming and chunked responses with LlamaIndex?
[05:31] Marcus: LlamaIndex + Redwood streaming works — we provide streaming chunks and callbacks to the vector store for incremental embedding writes. There's a short sample in the repo that shows LangChain streaming callback -> Redwood stream -> UI. We'll share the repo link.
[05:48] Alex: Are there any gotchas with LangChain memory or callback handlers if we go through your SDK vs raw REST?
[05:55] Marcus: Mostly around generator semantics — the SDK wraps streaming as an async iterator which LangChain can consume; older LangChain versions expect a different interface so you might need a thin adapter. We have example adapters for v0.0.240 and v1.x.
[06:14] Sofia: Priya, what are your current token volumes and model mix? That helps us size Dedicated recommendations.
[06:19] Priya: Currently about 80M tokens/month across a mix of chat-ish prompts and embeddings. Embeddings run on a separate pipeline. Token distribution: 60% short prompts (<200 tokens), 30% medium (200-800), 10% long sequences (>=2000).
[06:36] Marcus: Helpful. For that profile, Dedicated with dynamic batching + prefix caching could reduce unit costs, but if you prefer to avoid ops overhead hosted reserved capacity or a committed Dedicated pool may be simpler. We'll run cost sims.
[06:51] Alex: For a pilot, we want 1) integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex for RAG, 2) latency end-to-end under 200ms P95 for the chat path, 3) billing visibility and trace correlation. Can Redwood support a three-week pilot?
[07:06] Sofia: Yes, we typically do 2-4 week pilots. We'll scope it: Redwood Hosted with a dedicated reserved pool or a short-term Dedicated instance depending on latency needs. Pilot scope and SLAs will be in the follow-up doc.
[07:20] Tom: Network/firewall — our infra requires non-standard proxy headers and mTLS with client certs. Any examples?
[07:27] Marcus: We have examples for mTLS client cert usage and proxy passthrough in the SDK guide. In some cases teams run an internal sidecar that terminates client certs and forwards to Redwood with a signed header; we can provide reference code.
[07:44] Priya: About embeddings — will we be able to host our vector DB on-prem and only call Redwood for embeddings? We want to control the vector store.
[07:52] Marcus: Yes, that's common. Redwood can return embeddings over the API; you can then ingest into your on-prem vector DB. For Private deployments you can even run the embedding model in your VPC.
[08:03] Alex: Any limitations with function/tool calling or structured outputs? We plan to use function calling from the LLM to trigger downstream services.
[08:12] Marcus: Redwood supports structured outputs and function-like tool calls via our JSON schema enforcement and function-calling interface; streaming can carry partial function payloads for large outputs. We also support automatic fallback to non-streaming for strict ordering.
[08:30] Sofia: Quick question on SLAs — for Dedicated we provide latency/uptime SLAs. For Hosted we have best-effort but enterprise hosted customers can negotiate SLOs with reserved capacity.
[08:43] Alex: Pricing — can you share rough numbers for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go?
[08:49] Sofia: We'll send the full matrix, but rough: reserved Dedicated pool pricing is a commit with predictable unit costs and includes higher throughput targets; hosted pay-as-you-go is unit-priced with possible burstable rates. I'll include concrete examples based on your 80M tokens/month in the follow-up.
[09:05] Priya: On observability hooks again, do you provide example OpenTelemetry spans and a schema to map tokens to traces? We need to annotate request-level context for downstream APM.
[09:15] Marcus: Yes. We emit an otel-compatible trace with attributes for model, prompt_hash, token_count, and route. There's a sample collector config we can share to pipe into Jaeger.
[09:28] Tom: Is it possible to mask or redact prompt contents in logs for PII? Our security requires redaction at ingest.
[09:35] Marcus: You can configure redaction rules and enable scrubbing on the Console for hosted. For Private, you can choose to disable storage entirely or store logs encrypted with customer-managed KMS.
[09:50] Alex: Any existing customers in telecom/edge that used the LlamaIndex path that we could talk to?
[09:58] Sofia: We have references; I'll check and send a short list.
[10:04] Priya: One small thing — do you have a sample LangChain agent setup that shows reranking + embeddings + streaming? Our prototype mixes all three.
[10:12] Marcus: Yes, sample repo includes agents/rerank streaming example. I'll attach link in the follow-up email and drop a quick gist.
[10:23] Alex: Great. On integration testing — can we run a realistic load test with a sample model on Dedicated before committing?
[10:29] Marcus: Absolutely. We'll provide the benchmark harness and a pre-provisioned pool for testing. We ask customers to provide representative prompt sets and a data lake sample; Priya said she'd share token distributions.
[10:44] Priya: I'll share a sample set — but we'll scrub PII and replace with synthetic text.
[10:49] Sofia: Perfect. To wrap up, recap next steps...
[10:53] Marcus: Action items, I'll send benchmark template + repo links.
[10:57] Sofia: I'll send pricing, SOC2 and KMS docs and check references.
[11:01] Alex: We'll share token profiles and confirm pilot scope next week.
[11:06] Tom: I'll follow up on network constraints and proxy certs.
[11:10] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[11:12] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive week of 11/29.

End of call

Notes on transcription: some proper nouns may be slightly off (internal doc links abbreviated), and a couple of timestamps approximate. Recorded via Fireflies export.
